summary.text: A complex number has the form a + bi, where a and b are ordinary real numbers and i is the imaginary unit, a number that satisfies i² = −1.
Complex numbers extend the real numbers and still allow addition, subtraction, multiplication and division with the same familiar laws, which makes them a field.
They give solutions to all non-constant polynomial equations, even ones with no real solutions, and each complex number can be pictured as a point on a plane.

facts.label: Parts of 2 + 3i
facts.value: Real part is 2 and imaginary part is 3

facts.label: Real numbers inside
facts.value: A real number a is the complex number a + 0i

facts.label: Naming
facts.value: Square roots of negatives were named imaginary in the 17th century

facts.label: Multiplication on the plane
facts.value: Multiplying by a complex number scales and rotates the plane

facts.label: Absolute value
facts.value: The distance from the origin to the point

items.prompt: A friend argues that no number can be multiplied by itself to give a negative result, because positives and negatives both end up positive. How does the complex number system respond?

options.label: It redefines negative numbers so that they square to negatives
It bans negative numbers from the system altogether
It adds a new number i that satisfies i² = −1
It proves the friend's claim about positives is false

items.explain: Every nonzero real number squares to a positive number, so the system introduces the imaginary unit i, which satisfies i² = −1.

items.prompt: A complex number is a plain number plus a multiple of i. Which piece is called its imaginary part?

options.label: The real number that multiplies i, without the i itself
The whole second term, with the i included
The plain number that has no i attached
The sum of the two pieces added together

items.explain: For a + bi, the imaginary part is the real number b, not the complex number bi.

items.prompt: A teacher writes an everyday whole number such as nine on the board and asks whether it counts as a complex number. What is the right reply?

options.label: No, because its imaginary part is missing altogether
No, complex numbers must have a nonzero imaginary part
Yes, but only after it has been multiplied by i
Yes, it is that number plus 0i, with imaginary part 0

items.explain: The complex numbers extend the real numbers, and a real number a is regarded as the complex number a + 0i.

items.prompt: A drawing program stores each point as a complex number. What happens to the picture if every point is multiplied by the same complex number?

options.label: It slides across the page without turning
It is scaled and rotated
It is flipped over, like a mirror image
It stays exactly where it was before

items.explain: On the complex plane, multiplying by a complex number corresponds to scaling and rotation, while adding one corresponds to translation.

items.prompt: A point sits 3 units across and 4 units up on the complex plane. What does the absolute value of its complex number measure?

options.label: How far the point is from the origin
How tall the point stands over the horizontal axis
The angle the point makes with the positive real axis
Which side of the plane the point lies on

items.explain: By Pythagoras' theorem, the absolute value is the distance from the origin to the point. The angle is a different quantity, called the argument.

items.prompt: A complex number x + yi is multiplied by its conjugate, x − yi. What kind of number comes out?

options.label: Another number with a nonzero imaginary part
A purely imaginary number, such as 3i
A real number that is never negative, x² + y²
Always minus one, whatever x and y are

items.explain: The product (x + iy)(x − iy) equals x² + y², which is a non-negative real number.
